subject: Gen5 Lane D platform/Samsung contract: View-level ARR vote required alongside seamless surface vote

PRIMARY_FINDING=Current FoldOverlayView is a ViewGroup, but private FoldView is the actual invalidating RuntimeShader View. Android API35 ViewGroup requested-frame-rate votes do not propagate to child Views, and Android 15 ARR says most Views default Normal (~60Hz). Therefore a root SurfaceControl/window 120Hz vote is not sufficient by itself for this current View renderer: exact Gen5 visual-attempt ownership must also set 120/High on the actual FoldView, then reset it to DEFAULT at exact attempt end/replacement/abort.
PLATFORM_CORROBORATION=SurfaceControl.Transaction.setFrameRate may influence display refresh but Android explicitly says it does not directly affect the app frame-production pipeline. Use it as the seamless lower-layer vote, not proof of rendered cadence. Never use CHANGE_FRAME_RATE_ALWAYS.
API_LEVEL_CORRECTION=compileSdk35 can directly use View.setRequestedFrameRate (API35). FRAME_RATE_COMPATIBILITY_AT_LEAST and Display.hasArrSupport are API36 and must not be prerequisites for the first Gen5 experiment; evaluate after a separate compileSdk36 uplift.
SAMSUNG_BOUNDARY=Official Fold7 specs confirm both main and cover panels are adaptive 1-120Hz, but this does not prove One UI grants 120 in every fold topology/power/thermal/logical-display state. Log exact runtime mode + alternativeRefreshRates + FrameTimeline cadence.
PROOF=Existing FrameTimelineProbe/TransitionLab expected-presentation timing remains authoritative for requested-vs-effective cadence; request success and Display.mode are metadata only.
PERF=120Hz is incremental: one uniform-phase scheduling boundary improves mean next-vsync wait ~8.33ms->~4.17ms. Direct-vsync virtual hinge remains the major latency lever; legacy TiltFollower has a first-frame 1/60 assumption and should remain fallback.
